SUMMARY
No decision was reached. 5 open questions, 18 open blockers, 3 people took an explicit position on an option.

The meeting was a status walk-through of outstanding Technology Governance (TGov) deliverables, led by Jennifer Camarro with Danielle T. Benjamin, Robert T. Garnett, James Haskins, and Brandon M. O'Hara present; Neal was noted as out. Danielle asked Jennifer to report what was outstanding and who the blockers were so the group could work together to keep things moving. Jennifer said the list is "66% through," with some items complete and several stalled — chiefly those waiting on an ESG review or on Enterprise Architecture to respond to Prasad Edathil's repeated requests for clarification. Jennifer said she will keep ESG and procurement herself and farm out the rest; Danielle offered to take more than one item to reduce Jennifer's load, but no specific handoff list was confirmed. On the MSA, James Haskins asked whether it had to be fully executed before any pilot work could start; Jennifer said it is "very close to done" with red lines exchanged twice, but James Dodson has now moved it to a different reviewer, and Robert asked — and Jennifer confirmed — there is no hard legal disagreement holding it up, just completion.

## Presented, no challenge recorded

- James Haskins asked whether an MSA must be in place before any data-sharing or pilot work can begin.
- Jennifer Camarro said the MSA has gone back to the vendor and procurement twice and is close to done; the current holdup is a reviewer handoff.
- Jennifer Camarro said there is no hard disagreement with the vendor; both sides have been amendable, and the outstanding issue is simply moving it forward.
- Jennifer Camarro said the digital quality measure component will be deployed in Elevance's own environment and is not an open question.

## Open questions

- How to divide follow-up ownership of the remaining deliverable categories among the team (raised by Jennifer Camarro).
- Who should take over the architecture solution design task; Prasad Edathil cannot get Enterprise Architecture to say what they need (raised by Jennifer Camarro).
- How to sequence the two ESG components — digital quality measure and year-round chart collection — which can be independent or connected (raised by Jennifer Camarro).
- Whether a limited pilot agreement covering data sharing and testing is sufficient without a full MSA (raised by Jennifer Camarro).
- Whether the new TGov PowerPoint template applies to projects already in the approval process; Jennifer said she has asked twice and has not gotten a response (raised by Jennifer Camarro).

## Where people stand

- Jennifer Camarro: will keep ESG and procurement herself, farm out the rest, proposes she and Robert tag-team procurement, and agreed with Brandon that starting the chart-tool pilot in the vendor's Snowflake/Cloud environment is faster and lower cost.
- Danielle T. Benjamin: wants to get clear on what is outstanding and who Jennifer is waiting on so the group can align on how to work together; offered to take more than one item and to lean in where items group together naturally.
- Robert T. Garnett: asked whether a hard legal disagreement is holding up the MSA or whether it is just completion; did not decline Jennifer's proposal to tag-team procurement. Robert T. Garnett said "So that's good" on hearing there is no sticking point on the MSA.
- James Haskins: said Lilac does not use AI so faces a different barrier; offered his active daily Teams chat with Jay and Lauren as additional procurement support; said he and Vikram already filled out the PowerPoint template and is happy to do it again if required.
- Brandon M. O'Hara: proposed starting the pilot in the vendor's environment for speed, with a long-term plan to migrate to Elevance's environment once the engine component is ready.

## What is blocking progress

- Enterprise Architecture has not told Prasad Edathil what they need him to complete; Jennifer has followed up three to five times and a contact (Michael R.) has not replied (raised by Jennifer Camarro).
- The MSA has been moved to a different reviewer than originally expected, stalling its final completion (raised by Jennifer Camarro).
- The ESG team has not replied to the latest ESG submission, which is a dependency before enterprise security architecture can proceed (raised by Jennifer Camarro).
- At least one deliverable item's purpose and owner are unclear; Jennifer said she does not know what it is and has received no answer to repeated questions (raised by Jennifer Camarro).
- Whether the new TGov PowerPoint template is required for already-submitted projects is unanswered; Jennifer has asked twice with no response (raised by Jennifer Camarro).

## Next steps

- Jennifer Camarro will follow up again on Prasad Edathil's architecture solution design task.
- Jennifer Camarro will assign the architecture solution design task out and asked that someone take the Michael R. contact point.
- Jennifer Camarro said she and Robert T. Garnett will tag-team procurement to push the MSA to completion.
- Jennifer Camarro will divvy up the remaining items and the group will "relentlessly pursue them together."

## Awaiting a reply

- Jennifer Camarro asked James Haskins whether he had received a response about the TGov PowerPoint revamp applying to already-submitted projects; James said his team already filled it out with Vikram's help and offered to do it again, but did not confirm whether a response had been received.

## Things people asserted that others may want to check

- James Haskins said the Lilac product does not use AI, so the Responsible AI review does not apply to it.
- James Haskins said he speaks with the Lilac procurement contacts (Jay and Lauren) daily and has an active Teams chat with them.
- Brandon M. O'Hara said the vendor's preference is to host the tool in their own environment.
- Danielle T. Benjamin said Vikram is a peer of Anil and is relevant to who should be looped in for E3 support before additional people are added for visibility.
